newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Rate cut hopes to support Australian bonds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Rate cut hopes to support Australian bonds.

text.p: *The firm tone of Australian bonds continued as the U.S. market continues to strengthen on a subdued inflation outlook.
*Local market expected to remained supported by expectations of a near-term rate cut, with next week's wage and inflation data expected to be bond-friendly.

Expectations of a near-term rate cut are expected to provide a firm tone to Australian bonds this week, with an absence of major local data expected to keep the focus on next week's wages and inflation data and the U.S..

The market received a boost when U.S. 30-year Treasury yields fell to their lowest levels so far this year after a tame June producer price index helped confirm that U.S. inflation pressures remained contained.
That saw local bonds reverse Friday's movements, and although the market's tone should remain firm analysts said the fact a rate cut was fully priced in limited upside potential.
Last Thursday's highs of 93.415 on the 10-year and 94.26 on the three-year are expected to prove tough, with both contracts aprroaching overbought on their relative strength indices.
The three-year futures high saw the yield down near 5.50 percent -- the current official cash rate, while the 10-year's high saw the physical yield down to near 6.60 percent.

Westpac technical analyst Peter Pontikas said the three-year future's technicals were at the top end of their range, and moves above 94.20 would be hard to sustain. He saw moves by the 10-year futures to last week's high as selling opportunities.
